en.template: Help me decide whether to take a nursing job in {employer} while living in {town}. I am {age} with {experience} and take home about {pay}. The offer says {offer}. Rebuild the monthly comparison with my real figures, replace the assumed deduction rates with the ones I give you {rates}, run the stress test, and list what I should still ask for in writing. Flag anything unconfirmed. Ask before contacting anyone or submitting anything.

phases.title: Read the official Geneva and Swiss pages on the cross-border permit and diploma recognition, and fix the exchange rate
phases.judgment: It pinned down which body actually handles a nurse's French diploma (the Swiss Red Cross, not the medical-professions board) and openly flagged that it could not confirm the French nursing diploma is on the EU automatic-recognition list.

phases.title: Find the Geneva pay scale, health-insurance rules, tax treatment and commute costs, and write the guide
phases.judgment: A colleague checked the French health-insurance option against the official formula and corrected the rule as first described: it is 8% of (income from two years earlier minus 25% of the Social Security ceiling), about EUR 701 for 2027 on a July start with an assumed salary.

phases.title: Re-check contribution rates and rules, recompute every figure and test the layout
phases.judgment: No official page gave the Swiss pension and Geneva source-tax rates, so the net-pay figures use labelled 9% and 10% placeholders. Stress-tested: even if both are 10 points too low, the gain stays at about EUR 1,600 a month.

workers: Read the Geneva and Swiss pages on the cross-border permit and on recognition of a French nursing diploma, noting what could not be confirmed
